clue.text: Curtsy in front of oligarch entering B&B

indicators.note: the front letter goes inside, entering the pair of letters that B&B gives

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, gives its two Bs once the ampersand is dropped

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of oligarch is used

explanation.surface: A guest bows politely to a Russian tycoon checking into a guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' takes O from oligarch, and 'entering' puts it between the two Bs of B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick bob of the knees is a small curtsy, an old-fashioned gesture of respect.

clue.text: Short enticement plugging books?

indicators.note: to plug a gap is to fill it, so the shortened word fills the space between the two letters for books

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a lure is a bait or enticement

explanation.surface: Read as a whole, the clue describes the cover text that advertises a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the bait word, and 'plugging' sets the result between the two book abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The publisher's puff on a jacket is a brief come-on meant to sell the volume.

clue.text: Beat about the faces of excited dogs with moist kipper

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the synonym for beat goes round the initials

parts.note: to better a rival is to beat them

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone hits the excited dogs round the head and they end up with a soggy smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the faces of' takes the initials of three words; 'about' wraps the verb for beat around them. A kipper is a sleeper here, not a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is crossword slang for someone asleep, and a damp sleeper is a child who wets the bed.

clue.text: Initially, siblings' close relationship is mercurial — maybe getting on? Or brawling?

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each word in the run that follows it

parts.note: someone getting on in years is ageing, here in its shorter spelling

explanation.surface: A family pondering whether a tempestuous sibling bond comes with age or ends in fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of six words. 'mercurial' tempts you towards Hg, the symbol for mercury, but it only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrimmage is a confused scuffle, so taking part in one is fighting or brawling.

clue.text: For starters, southerners at restaurant eat fish

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Diners from the south begin their restaurant meal with a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Regret is Edith Piaf's way

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to regret it
Piaf was a French singer, and the French word for a street or way is ...

explanation.surface: Echoes Piaf's famous song about having no regrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing means feeling sorrow over a past act; in French the same word names a street, the road Piaf, a Parisian, would walk.

clue.text: One in revolutionary party supporting Jewish revolutionary's mother, father and nanny

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last

parts.note: Jesus, a Jewish teacher who upended religion, had Mary as his mother
pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the reversed party
revolutionary means turned round, so the party's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A political reading of a family tree: a revolutionary's mother and father backed by a radical party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the party round to PNS and 'in' puts the numeral inside, giving PINS; 'supporting' sets that beneath mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous fictional magical nursemaid of the Banks children is the archetypal nanny.

clue.text: Twisting narrow roads on which there's returning Royal Artillery Gunners

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that is on another sits above it, so it goes first
returning means coming back, so the abbreviation is read backwards
twisting means the letters of the synonym are wrung into a new order

parts.note: lanes are narrow country roads

explanation.surface: Gunners of the Royal Artillery come back along winding country lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the artillery abbreviation round, 'Twisting' rearranges the lanes, and 'on which there's' sets the first above the second. Arsenal is a London football club nicknamed the Gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: The north London football club Arsenal has the nickname Gunners, from its origins at the Woolwich munitions works.

clue.text: One leading judge is very angry

indicators.note: in a down clue the leading piece goes at the top, before the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: The senior member of a bench is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym describing someone furious or incensed.

clue.text: Policeman, cycling after environmentalist getting nicked — "'ello, 'ello, 'ello?"

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first in the answer
nicked means having a small bit cut away, so the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a green is an environmental campaigner

indicators.note: cycling sends the opening letter round to the back of the word

parts.note: Sting was the singer of the band The Police, so he is a Police man

explanation.surface: An eco-protester is arrested, and the bobby greets him with the stock phrase of British comic policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting nicked' cuts GREEN to GREE; 'cycling' turns STING into TINGS. ''ello, 'ello, 'ello' is the catchphrase of the stage British bobby, here read as a hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying hello three times is a run of salutations or welcomes.

clue.text: Franco/German articles on women's swimming are the first articles one gets into

definitions.text: the first articles one gets into

parts.note: un is a French article meaning a
der is the German article meaning the
W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about loosely, so the word are is rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece about French and German women's swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the three letters into EAR, which ends the run after the two foreign articles and the women's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes are the garments put on first when dressing, beneath everything else.

clue.text: Order second cold beer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for another chilled pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale is a graded series or ranking, an order of degrees.

clue.text: This particular section of Grimsby esplanade is so long

indicators.note: a section is a part of something, so the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A stretch of seafront at Grimsby, an English fishing port, goes on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across grimsBY Esplanade. 'so long' looks like a length but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye and so long are both casual farewells.

clue.text: Free-thinking writer suppressed by editor's boring cut

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the built piece goes inside the word for cut

parts.note: an indent is a notch or cut

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and contained, so the writer sits within the editor

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A free-spirited writer is censored by a dull editor who makes cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed by' makes EPEND; 'boring' drives that into the word for cut. 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent mind forms its own views, not bound by others.

clue.text: Altered deadline the source of antagonism for writer

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of deadline are put in a new order

parts.note: an enemy or foe is the one who stirs up hostility

explanation.surface: A writer finds his deadline moved and resents it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' rearranges DEADLINE into DANIELDE. 'the source of antagonism' looks like an initial-letter instruction but it is a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe was an English novelist and journalist, author of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Salesman's conversation with northern model

parts.note: patter is the slick talk of a salesman

explanation.surface: A sales rep chats up a model from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or design to copy from.

clue.text: Detailed documentary series I see in widescreen

indicators.note: detailed here means de-tailed, losing the final letter

parts.note: Panorama is a long-running BBC current affairs documentary programme
C sounds like see, a crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: Someone watching a thorough documentary series on a wide TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' is read as de-tailed, cutting PANORAMA to PANORAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoramic describes a broad, sweeping view, like a wide film format.

clue.text: One with a huge mouth a pencil fits

indicators.note: in fits means in spasms, so the letters of a pencil jerk into a new order

explanation.surface: Something with an enormous mouth can swallow a whole pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fits' is read as convulsions, not as matching.
explanation.definitionFit: This large water bird has a vast throat pouch that scoops up fish.

clue.text: Arrive carrying fish and chips

indicators.note: in a down clue the bearer holds up what it carries, so the fish sits on top

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to come in, arrive

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a takeaway of fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish and chips' reads as a meal, but 'chips' alone is the definition: one who chips at wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker chips and shapes timber, so one who chips is a joiner.

clue.text: Tell of the Emperor's leaders following close to deer in Nara

indicators.note: the leaders come after the rest in the answer
the letter from deer is placed inside the place name
the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter of deer is used
leaders are the front letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A guide describes the emperor's deer in Nara, a Japanese city famous for its tame deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives a letter put 'in' the city to make NARRA; 'leaders' gives two initials, 'following' it. Nara is a Japanese city famous for its tame deer park.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount a story, to tell it.

clue.text: The first two characters do a crossword for free

parts.note: the alphabet begins with A and B
to complete a crossword is to solve it

explanation.surface: Two people tackle a puzzle without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to release them from guilt, setting them free.

clue.text: Ships in Italy miles west of docks

indicators.note: in an across clue west is to the left, so these come first

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
ports are harbours with docks

explanation.surface: Italian ships berth some miles west of the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them into a country from abroad.

clue.text: Cost for getting letters delivered after, say, one gets returned

parts.note: post is a Latin-derived word meaning after, as in postwar

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the two short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg is short for for example, so say
a means one

explanation.surface: The price of sending letters, paid again when one comes back to the sender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets returned' turns the two short pieces round into AGE, which follows the Latin word for after.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the charge for sending mail.

clue.text: Dilapidated airsheds in which exhausted pill-poppers originally organised raves

indicators.note: the extra letters go inside the rearranged sheds
dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters of airsheds are rebuilt in a new order
exhausted means emptied out, so only the outer letters of pill-poppers survive
originally means at the start, so the first letter of organised

explanation.surface: Old aircraft hangars where tired drug users held illegal dance parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dilapidated' makes RHADISES; 'exhausted' and 'originally' give three letters, put 'in which' after its third letter. 'raves' looks like parties but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodising is gushing with enthusiasm, raving about something.

clue.text: Bonus feature put on after trailer?

indicators.note: the clothing verb comes after the advert piece

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement, an ad, for a film
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: An extra on a DVD released after the preview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' is a film preview, so an ad, not a towed vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item bundled with something.

clue.text: Big Bird and Elmo? Just odd characters suitable for kids

indicators.note: the odd characters are the first, third and so on, so alternate letters of Elmo

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal, fit for children

explanation.surface: Two Sesame Street puppets, the giant yellow bird and furry red monster, are fine for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Bird and Elmo are Sesame Street puppets, but 'Big Bird' is the definition: a large flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a huge flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Man up the tree that's dirty, having wiped a gibbon's bottom

indicators.note: wiped means cleaned away, so those letters are removed from the word for dirty

parts.note: unclean means dirty

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the last letter of gibbon

explanation.surface: A grubby man up a tree cleans a gibbon's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having wiped' removes A and N (gibbon's 'bottom') from UNCLEAN. 'tree' means a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree places a parent's brother as a male relative in the generation above.

clue.text: Caught butt in circular bit of gold?

indicators.note: caught means picked up by ear, signalling that the phrase sounds like the answer

parts.note: to meddle is to butt in, to interfere

explanation.surface: Someone stopped while interfering in a gold coin's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is a hearing word: the word said aloud for 'butt in' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is a round metal disc given as an award.

clue.text: Mega fan thanks almost all staff

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word for staff is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a stick is a staff or walking pole

explanation.surface: A keen supporter thanks nearly every member of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega and fantastic are both slang words of enthusiastic praise, meaning terrific.

clue.text: New degree in Sports Enterprise

parts.note: BA is the Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A fresh qualification in business studies about sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Basketball Association is a US professional league run as a business.

clue.text: Allied force, invading with Italian and English, then retreating, embarrassed and worried

indicators.note: invading means entering, so the letter for force goes into the next pieces

parts.note: con is Italian for with
F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red, as in blushing, means embarrassed
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A military narrative: a force invades with Italians and English, then pulls back in shame and anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' puts the force letter inside CONE; 'retreating' turns the blush colour into DER. 'force' looks like an army but is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Confederate means joined in league or alliance with others.

clue.text: Some geordies flipping eggs

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters found are read backwards
some means part of, so the letters are taken from inside geordies

explanation.surface: A few people from Newcastle, England, toss fried eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds EOR inside geORdies, and 'flipping' turns it round. Geordies are people from Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish.
